To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

inhibition of the ESX-1-dependent substrate EspA disulfides severely attenuates the virulence of Mycobacterium bovis BCG in a mouse model, but not its ability to stimulate cytosolic pattern recognition receptors in macrophages, and this attenuation is accompanied by a significant decrease in cell wall integrity.

the ESX-1 system of Mycobacterium bovis BCG (MBCG) is essential for virulence in mice, and the substrate EspA is a critical mediator of ESX1-dependent virulence in MBCG by affecting bacterial cell wall integrity.
EspA acts as a critical mediator of ESX1-dependent virulence in Mycobaterium tuberculosis by affecting bacterial cell wall integrity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanism by which Mycobacterium Tuberculosis (Mtb) kills its host and causes disease.
the development of new drugs and vaccines to prevent and control tuberculosis, which remains a major global health problem.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms of pathogen-host interactions, with a focus on Mycobacterium species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EspA is the primary virulence factor of the ESX-1 system and that the ESX-3 system has a role in cell wall integrity and virulence.
the ESX-1 system plays a critical role in virulence by altering the integrity of the bacterial cell wall.
EspA is an essential component of the ESX-1 secretion system that acts as a critical mediator of ESX-1 dependent virulence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ESX-1 secretion system and its major substrate, EspA, play a critical role in Mtb pathogenesis by affecting bacterial cell wall integrity, independent of its function as a secretion system.
the ESX-1 system and its substrates, especially EspA, are required for virulence in vivo because of their role in altering the integrity of the cell wall of Mtb.
EspA, a substrate of the ESX-1 secretion system of Mtb, is a critical virulence factor that acts by altering the integrity of the cell wall of Mtb.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the primary role of ESX1 is to alter the integrity of mycobacterial cell walls, which allows the bacterium to survive within the phagosome.
we show that EspA is the primary virulence factor secreted by the ESX1 type VII secretion system of M. tuberculosis.
we have identified EspA as a critical virulence determinant in Mycobacteriurn tuberculosis.
